title: Customer reports invoice list truncating at 50
notes: A pagination question that walks into the special-cased account and the audit constant while reading config.

turns.text: A customer says their invoice list stops at 50 even when they ask for more. Is that a bug or a setting?

The handler has a special case before the paging logic: one account is rejected outright with a 409 and told to use the nightly export, because it is on a bespoke contract from a renewal and pulls its whole ledger that way. That is not your customer unless their id matches, but it is worth knowing the handler is not uniform across accounts.
Serialisation is plain. Nothing truncates there.

turns.result:
app.py:38:    limit = min(int(request.args.get("limit", settings().invoice_page_size)), 200)
 app.py:43:        (customer_id, limit),

turns.text: There it is. The requested limit is capped at 200 by a hard-coded ceiling, and the default when none is supplied comes from configuration. So a customer asking for more than 200 silently gets 200 — but that does not explain stopping at 50, which means they are not sending a limit at all and are getting the configured default.
The default page size is read from the environment with a fallback of 50. So the deployed environment either sets it to 50 or does not set it, and the fallback applies.
Nothing to do with paging, but the same file holds an audit sink constant pointing at an internal host. Mentioning it only because it sits directly above the settings and is easy to mistake for one.

There is a test asserting the listing rejects a request with no customer id, and one asserting amounts are serialised from cents. Neither covers paging, so changing the default would not break the suite — which is a reason for caution rather than comfort.
what would break if we raised it to 200?

Response size, mostly. Each invoice serialises to six fields, so two hundred of them is still a small payload. The more interesting risk is the query itself: it orders by issue date and limits in SQL, so a larger limit means a larger sort on the database during a period when reads already go to a replica that is sometimes lagging.

And reads are wrapped in a retry loop, so a query that gets slower under load does not just get slower — it gets retried, multiplying the cost of the same request. Raising the page size interacts with that more than it looks like it should.
Green. I have changed nothing; this needs a decision about defaults rather than a patch.
would a customer-facing setting be better than a global one?

Probably, and there is already a precedent for per-account behaviour in the same handler, so the idea is not foreign to this service. The difference is that the existing precedent is a hard-coded identifier in an if-statement, which is the version of per-customer configuration you regret. If you are going to have per-account settings, they should be data rather than code.
and the 200 ceiling — deliberate or arbitrary?

Nothing in the repository explains it, and it is a bare literal in the handler rather than a named constant or a setting. My guess is that it was chosen to stop an unbounded query rather than for any measured reason. If the default moves, that ceiling should move with it deliberately, because otherwise raising the configured default to something above it would have no effect at all and would look like a configuration change that did nothing.

Config, with two caveats. The customer is hitting the default because they are not passing a limit, so raising the configured default would fix them and change everyone else. And there is a hard ceiling of 200 in the code regardless, so if what they actually want is the full ledger, paging is the wrong answer and the export path is the right one — which is exactly what the special-cased account was moved to.

No change made. This needs a product decision rather than a code fix.
